Know before you go

Getting around

  • Trains: buy on cp.pt. Porto–Lisbon is €35.70 on the Alfa Pendular. Sale fares need 5+ days' notice.
  • Lisbon transit: a 24-hour Carris/Metro/CP ticket is €11.40 and covers the Sintra train. A 72-hour Lisboa Card (€62) also covers the castle, Jerónimos, Belém Tower and Tram 28. On this plan it saves only about €10 each, more if you add museums.
  • Transit cards: everyone needs their own; one card can't pay for the group. Porto: a blue Andante card (€0.60) from the ticket machines at the airport metro station, loaded with a Z4 ride for the airport and Z2 rides in town, or a 24-hour Andante Tour pass. Lisbon: a navegante occasional card (€0.50) from the machines at any metro station, such as Oriente or the airport, loaded with Zapping credit or the 24-hour ticket. A Lisbon card holds one kind of ticket at a time, so use up the Zapping credit before loading a 24-hour ticket.
  • Rides: for 10 people, plan on three Ubers, Bolts or taxis. In Lisbon a ride home from Alfama or Chiado is about 10 minutes and under €10 a car.

Entry to Europe

  • New border check (EES): the EU now takes fingerprints and a photo the first time you enter, so expect slower passport queues landing in Porto and leaving Lisbon. The plan allows for both.
  • ETIAS isn't needed yet: as of early November 2026 the EU hadn't announced a start date for the online travel authorization. Check the official ETIAS site the week before you fly.
  • Passports must be valid for at least 3 months after Dec 20.

December weather and safety

  • Rain: December is one of Porto's wettest months. Bring rain jackets; each outdoor day has a rainy-day swap.
  • Shoes with grip: Lisbon's polished stone pavements and Porto's granite hills are very slippery when wet.
  • Cold nights: colder still at Jardim do Morro and on the ferry. Portuguese flats often have weak heating, so ask both hosts about heaters.
  • Pickpockets: watch bags on Tram 28, the Lisbon metro, Rossio and Ribeira.
  • Recheck in late November: Wonderland Lisboa's opening, the Rossio Christmas market dates, Clérigos night tickets, the Gulbenkian's Saturday hours and price, Ponto Final's winter closing, and any rail or metro strikes.

Language

Nearly everything on this plan works in English; anything that doesn't is tagged in the day plan. The Google Translate camera handles menus and signs, Chrome translates Portuguese websites, and your Airbnb hosts can call restaurants for you. "Obrigado" (men) or "obrigada" (women) means thank you.

Also worth trying

  • Bacalhau: salted cod, cooked many ways. Try bacalhau à Brás (shredded with egg and fried potato) or com natas (baked in cream). It's the traditional Christmas Eve dish.
  • Seafood: clams, octopus and grilled fish. Grilled sardines are a summer dish, so they're harder to find in December.
  • Coffee: an espresso is a bica in Lisbon and a cimbalino in Porto. A galão is milky coffee in a glass.
